newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Low volume leaves Bund vols vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Low volume leaves Bund vols vulnerable.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options on LIFFE slipped back on Tuesday, but traders said the limited volume of trading has left the market vulnerable.
Bund options' volatility rose sharply above the 6.0 percent level late last week, sparked by fluctuations in the underlying futures market.
It has been sliding since the release of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report last Friday, as a lower-than-expected number took the heat out of the market.
"Volatility is starting to come off, but the problem with selling it when volume is this thin is that you can get caught in a short squeeze," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London.
March Bund futures were down seven basis points at 100.70 by 1435 GMT.

January serial options on the March contract were trading at a volatility of 5.70 percent, down from 5.80 percent from midday on Monday. February volatility dipped to 5.75 percent, from 5.89 percent and March volatility fell to 5.35 percent from 5.90.
A trader at a British bank said a trade of 1,000 out-of-the money straddles sold by a U.S. bank was the most noticeable feature of the day's trade.
Also, another British bank bought 1,000 lots of out-of-the-money straddles.
However, traders said investors are displaying reluctance to come into the market, with some still licking their wounds from last week, and others unwilling to take risks ahead of year end.
Activity was clustered around the 101.00 and 101.50 strikes in January, and around the 100.00 strike in February. March saw most volume in the 101.00 and 102.00 strikes.
